key_insight: The Hankel neural operator (HNO) combines rational-kernel convolution with finite-rank boundary corrections to learn differential-equation solution operators beyond periodic Fourier representations.
engineering_relevance: HNO offers a promising surrogate for fluid and transport simulations where boundaries, transients and grid refinement challenge standard Fourier neural operators.
method: Derives a Toeplitz-plus-Hankel representation for well-posed linear constant-coefficient boundary-value problems.
Implements non-periodic FFT convolution, including a causal form, and closed-loop dynamics without fading memory.
Provides a rational Fourier multiplier that includes FNO as a special case.
evidence_signal: HNO achieved the lowest mean test error across nine LNO benchmarks and the Burgers, Darcy and Navier–Stokes FNO benchmarks; its Darcy error stayed nearly constant from 85² to 421² grids while FNO's grew eightfold.
watch_item: The structural theorem covers linear constant-coefficient problems, and some benchmark improvements—including parameter-matched Navier–Stokes—were not statistically significant.
paper_title: Beyond Fourier and Laplace: The Hankel Neural Operator for Learning Solution Operators of Differential Equations
